key_insight: Dialogue re-cinematography turns one wide-angle recording into multiple cinematic views. The paper proposes grounding shot synthesis in audio to address lip-motion errors when the original video provides weak visual cues.
problem_solved: Filming close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder coverage is costly. Generating these views from a single recording is challenging because visually driven models struggle with speech-related lip motion when faces are small or obscured.
method: Use a single wide-angle dialogue video as the source for additional shots.
Ground shot synthesis in dialogue audio rather than relying on visual cues alone.
Target speech-consistent lip motion across generated views; architecture and evaluation details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: This approach could reduce the need for multi-camera dialogue capture and support AI-assisted editing. For practitioners, it highlights audio as an important conditioning signal when visual evidence of speech is limited.
visual_elements: One wide-angle source frame branching into close-up, medium, and over-the-shoulder views.
A pipeline diagram showing source video and audio feeding a shot-synthesis model.
An audio waveform aligned with a sequence of generated mouth movements.
A visual-only versus audio-grounded comparison labeled as a conceptual illustration, not reported results.
paper_title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
paper_authors: Anthony Chen, Naomi Ken Korem, Matan Ben-Yosef, Tavi Halperin, Urska Jelercic
